content.text: The Aga Khan University Medical College was established in 1983, as a part of the Aga Khan University’s Faculty of Health Sciences in Karachi, Pakistan. It works closely with the School of Nursing and Midwifery and the University Hospital to produce excellence in educational programmes and medical practice.

Faculty, students and staff are devoted to the highest standard of education, scholarship and research. The faculty also provides the highest level of patient care through collaboration with various health care professionals and use of state-of-the-art equipment to support diagnosis and treatment in the University Hospital.

Health related research has always been a high priority activity of AKU. For the Medical College (being a part of AKU’s Faculty of Health Sciences), the over-arching theme is '
Social and Economic Determinants of Health
' (SEDOH), the current shorthand for describing health approaches that move beyond biomedical and behavioral risk factor approaches to health promotion. This includes:
Maternal and newborn child health
Non-communicable diseases
Infection, immunity and inflammation
Human development
Neurosciences
Stem cell biology

Research in AKU’s Medical College spans many disciplines but particularly emphasises problems of the developing world, such as investigation of the causes and treatment of childhood diarrhoea, studies of the immunological characteristics of tuberculosis and leprosy, and community-based health systems development.
Several initiatives are in place to support  and strengthen research at the Medical College.
(details to be shared soon)

Our distinguished faculty are champions of life long learning. They mentor students to build problem solving and collaboration skills that will enable them to become leaders in research and healthcare service.

content.text: The AKU Medical College, Pakistan was recently conferred with ASPIRE Excellence Awards in Student Assessment and Student Engagement in the Curriculum at the Association for Medical Education in Europe (AMEE) Conference 2013 held in Prague, Czech Republic.
The Medical College, Pakistan aims to:
Enhance, strengthen, and expand our educational programs
Broaden existing medical and nursing curricula
Enhance our research capability, productivity, and impact
Strengthen and support our faculty, staff, and students
Enhance teaching/learning and campus life experience of our faculty and students
Contribute to the development of an integrated healthcare system
Foster collaboration and integration locally, regionally, and globally
Build our Infrastructure and funding base
French Medical Institute for Children (FMIC), Kabul

Considering the urgent need for quality health care in war-stricken Afghanistan and the University’s mandate of serving the developing world, the Medical College, Pakistan, in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health, Afghanistan, has initiated residency programmes in Paediatric Medicine, Paediatric Surgery, Anaesthesiology, Pathology, Radiology, Cardiology and Orthopaedics at the French Medical Institute for Children (FMIC), Kabul, Afghanistan. FMIC is currently an 85-bedded paediatric health care facility managed by AKU under a partnership between the Governments of Afghanistan and France, Aga Khan Development Network and La Chaine de L’Espoir, a French humanitarian organisation. Over the next two years, FMIC will expand into a 150-bedded mother and child complex.
University of California (UCSF), San Francisco

The Medical College is cognisant of the fact that contribution to knowledge society is the hallmark of all leading academic institutions of the world. Therefore, in our continued journey to be a truly research-led University of the 21st century, we continue to foster our research capacities and forge new multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary research collaborations. One such collaboration is with University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), on a five-year start-up plan on Stem Cell Science and Stem Cell Therapies programme. UCSF, one of the leading research universities in this area, will assist AKU in developing critical capacity and bridging the gap between clinicians and basic/clinical scientists in stem cell research. AKU’s Centre for Regenerative Medicine will focus on the study of stem cells, with the aim of developing new treatments for major diseases, including cancer, heart disease, diabetes, wound healing, musculoskeletal diseases, degenerative diseases, and liver failure. It will seek to translate innovative laboratory research into clinical and commercial arenas to replace and repair diseased tissues and organs.

The office has received the ethical review committee approval and will soon start the study. Further updates will be shared as the project progresses.

AKU tops HEC ranking for medical universities
The Aga Khan University has maintained its position as the top medical university in Pakistan for the fifth time in a row in the ranking released by the
Higher Education Commission
– the primary regulatory body of higher education in the country.
Read more...
International recognition for excellence in medical education
The Aga Khan University's Medical College received two ASPIRE awards – for international excellence in education in a medical school – from the
Association for Medical Education in Europe

in Prague, Czech Republic, standing out as an eminent leader in medical education among global universities. The awards were given to recognize the high standards AKU has demonstrated in the areas of student engagement and student assessment over the years while producing graduates of international caliber.
Read more...
MacJannet Prize for Global Citizenship awarded to AKU Medical College's Urban Health Programme
The
Talloires Network
and the
MacJannet Foundation

today announced the winners of the first annual MacJannet Prize for Global Citizenship. The first place winner is the Urban Health Programme based in Aga Khan University in Pakistan. This innovative and long-standing program run by AKU Medical College's
Department of Community Health Sciences
provides critical health and socio-economic support to the squatter settlements of Karachi.
Read more...
Every Gift Matters

As the University explores and embarks upon new challenging endeavors, it will rely heavily on the encouragement and contributions of its supporters and well-wishers to sustain the activities of medical students, residents, fellows and graduate students at the University, as well as provide an opportunity for non-AKU physicians and other allied health professionals practicing in Pakistan to attend AKU-sponsored non-degree clinical education and training programmes.

You have the opportunity to make an investment in the future of the Medical College. Your commitment will help to ensure that deserving, talented students are able to expand their intellectual and socio-economic horizons at the University.

Your generosity will touch the life of a young man or woman … mean the world to a family … transform an entire community. Your gift is more than just a means to an education. It is an investment in talent and in the future.
Upon leaving the University, our students expect to change the world; we expect it, too.
Thanks to you.

body.title: 1-Year Post Graduate Certification in Maintenance and Clinical Engineering Functions

content.text: Department: Biomedical Engineering in Collaboration with Office of Allied Health
Course Duration: 1 year
Class Timings: Evening Classes (Ideal for working professionals)
Entity: Aga Khan University Hospital
Location: Stadium Road, Karachi Pakistan

The Biomedical Department at Aga Khan University Hospital has embarked on the development of an innovative educational program titled the Certification in Maintenance and Clinical Engineering Functions-Biomedical. This program aims to address the significant gap between academic knowledge and industry demands in the field of biomedical engineering within Pakistan. After thorough deliberation and consultation with university leadership, industry experts, and the Industry Advisory Board, it became evident that there is a pressing need for a program that equips students with the specific skills required by the biomedical engineering industry.
Who Should Apply?
• Holders of B.S / B.E in Biomedical Engineering
• Minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale.
• Good interpersonal skills, particularly communication skills
• Excellent problem-solving skills, with an emphasis on practical application in clinical settings.
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment.
• Commitment to continuous learning and professional development within the field of biomedical engineering.
Program Highlights:
• Practical training with real hospital equipment
• Industry-focused curriculum
• Evening classes to suit working professionals
• Learn from experienced biomedical engineers
• Certification from a leading healthcare institution
Program Fees:
• Total Course Fee: PKR 300,000/- (inclusive of all taxes) Pay in Easy Instalments! ​
• Registration Fee: None

Why Enroll? Step into the cutting-edge world of biomedical innovation! This unique Post Graduate Certification bridges the critical gap between academic knowledge and real-world industry demands. Tailored for aspiring and early-career Biomedical Engineers, this program combines intensive academic instruction with hands-on clinical training, empowering you with the skills needed to thrive in hospitals, diagnostics labs, and biomedical equipment service environments. Register and secure your seats and immerse yourself in the ever-evolving world of technology.

Payment Guideline.pdf

faryal.hamza@aku.edu
For any queries, email at the same address.

As the first Associate Dean of Allied Health, I am honored to welcome you to the Office of Allied Health (OAH) website and lead a community of dedicated individuals passionate about the health and well-being of others.

The Office of Allied Health is committed to providing quality education, research, and service in the field of Allied Health Sciences. We offer various programmes and courses to equip our students with the knowledge, skills, and practical experience necessary to excel in their chosen professions. In AKU Karachi, 22 allied health programs enrolling 100 plus trainees are currently managed and organized by 12 departments. Through our state-of-the-art facilities, laboratories, and clinical partnerships, we provide hands-on training opportunities that prepare our students for real-world challenges. Whether you are studying to become a medical laboratory technologist, a radiology technologist, an anesthesia technologist, or any other allied health professional, we are committed to helping you achieve your goals. We encourage our students to participate in research activities, as it enhances their educational experience and prepares them to be leaders in their fields.
The provision of high-quality service is a core value of our training programmes, and we strive to make a positive impact on the community that we serve.

I invite you to explore our website to learn more about our programmes, student activities, faculty, research initiatives, and community involvement. Whether you are a prospective student, a current student, an alum, or a community member, we are here to support you and provide the resources you need. I encourage you to reach out to us with any questions or inquiries.
We look forward to welcoming you into our vibrant and caring community.
Warm Regards,
Dr Robyna Irshad Khan
Associate Dean, Office of Allied Health​​
